title: Crypto liquidations jump to $1.57 billion as Binance hack sends bitcoin, ether lower
content: Bitcoin traded near $77,350 after $6.3 billion Binance hack, with crypto futures liquidations jumping to $1.57 billion.

title: Binance loses over $6 billion in 'biggest crypto hack in history'
content: Crypto prices are sliding on the news, with bitcoin falling back to $77,000, though Binance's co-CEO said it would cover all losses.
summary: Binance has experienced the largest cryptocurrency hack in history, losing an astounding $5.7 billion. This significant event has caused a downturn in the crypto market, with Bitcoin's value notably falling to $79,000.

title: Binance uncovers wider breach in $6.3 billion exploit, targets Sunday withdrawal restart
content: CEO Richard Teng said hackers erased evidence and bypassed security checks. Binance plans to publish its proof of reserves Monday.
summary: Binance CEO Richard Teng revealed a wider breach in a $6.3 billion exploit, noting that hackers erased evidence and bypassed security checks. The exchange aims to restart withdrawals on Sunday and plans to publish its proof of reserves on Monday.

title: Binance arranges $6.34 billion to cover losses from record crypto hack
content: Binance said it reserved its own funds to cover the $6.3 billion hack, including freezes of roughly $3 billion in stolen assets.
summary: Binance has allocated $6.34 billion of its own funds to cover losses from a record cryptocurrency hack. This fund allocation includes the successful freezing of approximately $3 billion in stolen assets, ensuring coverage for the significant breach.

title: Wall Street analysts urge investors to buy crypto stocks after $6.3 billion Binance hack

summary: Wall Street analysts are advising investors to buy crypto stocks despite a massive $6.3 billion Binance hack. Firms like Cantor Fitzgerald, TD Cowen, and Compass Point believe this significant incident will not derail the crypto market's ongoing recovery.

title: Here’s how an Ethereum upgrade helped drain part of Binance’s $6 billion loss
content: On Ethereum, the attacker used a 2025 upgrade built to make ordinary wallets smarter, armed with 50 signatures from Binance's own wallet.
summary: An attacker exploited an upcoming 2025 Ethereum upgrade, designed to enhance smart wallets, by leveraging 50 signatures from Binance's own wallet. This method contributed to a portion of Binance's reported $6 billion loss. The incident highlights the security implications of new blockchain features and wallet vulnerabilities.

title: Polymarket suspends trading after third-party breach leads to user losses
content: Polymarket said one of its third-party providers was breached after users reported seeing their accounts drained.

title: Google’s satellite AI server transmits its first response to Earth
content:
Google's AI chip-equipped satellite has generated its first response from space. In a blog post on Friday, Google says it successfully booted up the satellite's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), allowing the on-board Gemma 4 model to follow through on a prompt to create a haiku about being in space:
Blue marble below
Data streams in silent grace
Starlight feeds my core. ✨
Google says it tried out other space-themed limericks and telemetry prompts as well. The test is part of Google's Project Suncatcher, an experimental initiative that could eventually put AI data centers in space. Google launched the satellite into orbit earlier this …
Read the full story at The Verge.

title: Starbucks wants to use AI to show you a ‘personalized digital menu’ at the drive-thru
content:
Starbucks could eventually show you a personalized digital menu when you pull up to the drive-thru. During an earnings call on Thursday, Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol said the company is going to explore "experiences that recognize participating customers as they arrive, present personalized digital menus, and make payment more effortless," as spotted earlier by More Perfect Union.
It sounds similar to the technology that Taco Bell is experimenting with, which could change the layout, content, and visuals on a digital menu board "on a car-by-car basis." McDonald's also recently showed off an AI-powered feature it's piloting at a handful of dri …

title: Pope Leo calls for the disarmament of AI: ‘Machines are tools, not persons’
content:
Pope Leo XIV says AI systems should be "disarmed," adding that humans "have the responsibility to guide, change and, when necessary, reject its applications." In Friday's Papal Address, Pope Leo encourages United Nations member states to "take concrete steps toward banning lethal autonomous weapons" during their meeting in Geneva next month.
The address reflects many of the ideas Pope Leo laid out in his first major papal document in May, which highlighted "safeguarding the human person in the time of artificial intelligence." title: Silicon Valley wants you to invest in miracles
content:
Investing in any stock is kind of like gambling in the sense that you're betting your money on a company's future performance. But how do you bet on a technology that could, in the worst-case scenario, "pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity," or best case, "bring forth an age of miracles"?
To some extent, Anthropic suggests in a letter at the top of its S-1 filing, you have to just believe.
Anthropic's 335-page S-1 prospectus, filed Monday, is part of a steady hype escalation in Silicon Valley's interactions with Wall Street. In some ways, it's not even that bizarre; SpaceX IPO'd in June after filing an S-1 that referenced din …
Read the full story at The Verge.

title: Sam Altman sympathizes with mathematicians, but says OpenAI’s math onslaught won’t stop
content:
After months of bombarding mathematicians  with a relentless stream of AI-generated results, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says he sympathizes with researchers struggling to make sense of it all. But he has no intention of stopping - and hints there could be much more to come from the company's stockpile of discoveries.
"I think, on net, the world deserves to understand how the universe works," Altman said during an episode of the Cheeky Pint podcast released Thursday. "But I do have empathy for the method."

His comments mark one of the first times the OpenAI chief has directly acknowledged the company's impact on mathematicians, following a strin …

title: Maine’s data center revolt will decide who controls the Senate
content:
Maine Sen. Susan Collins, a Republican, was midway through defending her record during the final debate of the midterms when an audience member cut her short.
"I'm terrified," a man shouted. "AI data centers are destroying our climate. They are poisoning our water."  Collins brushed off the outburst, tying the man to her Democratic challenger, Troy Jackson. But the fear echoing through the auditorium wasn't so easily dismissed. Just days before voters head to the polls, the rapid expansion of resource-hungry data centers has exploded into one of Maine's most volatile campaign issues.

title: Wikipedia’s operator says a bad AI copyright ruling could threaten the open web
content:
The Wikimedia Foundation is staking out a middle ground in a group of landmark AI copyright cases, pushing courts to legally protect large language models (LLMs) training on copyrighted work - but not chatbots regurgitating that work to users. An overly black-and-white ruling, it says, could either deprive Wikipedians of useful AI-based tools or endanger the open web.

title: You can generate and edit Google Docs files directly in Gemini chats now
content:
Now you can generate, preview, and edit PDFs, Google Docs, Google Sheets, slide decks, Markdown files, TXT files, and code directly within Google Gemini. The new file editing capabilities are available starting today for all Gemini users, and while PDF previews/editing works on both the web and mobile, all other file formats are only in the web version for now.
Google added support for generating and downloading files in Gemini earlier this year, but now you can tweak those files without leaving the Gemini app. Google says you can expand documents to edit them in full-screen mode and highlight text in files to ask Gemini questions or prompt …

title: Microsoft’s AI future has fewer jobs
content:
To anyone listening closely to what Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has been saying over the past couple of years, this week felt like the clearest sign yet that AI is about to fundamentally change the size of Microsoft's workforce. Microsoft is now offering voluntary buyouts to around 60,000 employees across the US, UK, Canada, and India.
It's the first time the company has presented such an offer to so many employees, expanding greatly upon the retirement offer that was limited to around 9,000 employees earlier this year. It's all part of an ongoing effort to avoid reducing investment in AI infrastructure by lowering Microsoft's operating cos …

title: The NYT Cooking app is testing AI recipe modifications
content:
The AI tool provides recommendations and adjusts the recipe accordingly. | Image: The New York Times	

The New York Times is testing a new AI feature for its Cooking app that helps users to modify recipes, and it has sparked some drama among users. Last Friday, NYT Cooking senior editor Genevieve Ko announced the feature, which can be used to recommend substitutions for ingredients and cooking equipment, scale recipes to any number of servings, and "generally make our recipes work for what a cook needs at that moment."
